questions.stem: This diagram of the heart wall and its coverings shows a fluid-filled space between two serous membranes. What is the primary physiologic function of this space and its fluid?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It conducts the electrical impulse from SA to AV node

choices.label: B
choices.text: It provides lubricating serous fluid that lets the beating heart move with minimal friction

choices.label: C
choices.text: It stores oxygenated blood for coronary perfusion

choices.label: D
choices.text: It anchors the chordae tendineae to the papillary muscles

choices.label: E
choices.text: It secretes hormones that regulate heart rate

explanation.summary: The pericardial cavity, between the visceral and parietal serous pericardium, holds a small volume of serous fluid that lubricates the surfaces so the heart can contract and relax with minimal friction.
explanation.whyCorrect: The pericardial cavity, between the visceral and parietal serous pericardium, holds a small volume of serous fluid that lubricates the surfaces so the heart can contract and relax with minimal friction.

questions.stem: This muscle tissue is composed of branching cells joined end to end, each with a single central nucleus and abundant pink cytoplasm, supported by delicate connective tissue and capillaries. What tissue is this?

explanation.summary: Branching fibers with single central nuclei and interposed capillaries are diagnostic of cardiac muscle, distinguishing it from multinucleated peripheral-nucleus skeletal muscle and spindle-shaped smooth muscle.
explanation.whyCorrect: Branching fibers with single central nuclei and interposed capillaries are diagnostic of cardiac muscle, distinguishing it from multinucleated peripheral-nucleus skeletal muscle and spindle-shaped smooth muscle.

questions.stem: The magnified inset (red arrow) highlights a darker transverse band crossing a cardiac muscle fiber at the junction between two cells. What structure is indicated, and what is its function?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A motor end plate transmitting nerve impulses to the fiber

choices.label: B
choices.text: A band of collagen anchoring the cell to the endomysium

choices.label: C
choices.text: A T-tubule invagination triggering calcium release

choices.label: D
choices.text: An intercalated disc, which mechanically couples cardiomyocytes and electrically couples them via gap junctions

choices.label: E
choices.text: A Z-line marking the boundary of a single sarcomere

explanation.summary: Intercalated discs are specialized step-like junctions between cardiomyocytes containing desmosomes/fasciae adherentes (mechanical linkage) and gap junctions (electrical continuity), enabling the myocardium to contract as a functional syncytium.
explanation.whyCorrect: Intercalated discs are specialized step-like junctions between cardiomyocytes containing desmosomes/fasciae adherentes (mechanical linkage) and gap junctions (electrical continuity), enabling the myocardium to contract as a functional syncytium.

questions.stem: In this section of the outer heart wall, the surface (Ep) is covered by a mesothelium (Mes) over connective tissue containing a nerve (N) and fat (F), sitting directly on cardiac muscle (M). Which layer of the heart wall is bracketed as Ep?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Tunica media of a coronary artery

explanation.summary: The outer surface mesothelium overlying loose connective tissue, adipose, nerves and vessels directly on myocardium is the epicardium, i.e. the visceral layer of the serous pericardium.
explanation.whyCorrect: The outer surface mesothelium overlying loose connective tissue, adipose, nerves and vessels directly on myocardium is the epicardium, i.e. the visceral layer of the serous pericardium.

questions.stem: This diagram of the heart wall shows three tissue layers plus an outer sac. Which layer lines the internal chambers and is continuous with the endothelium of the great vessels?

explanation.summary: The endocardium is the innermost layer lining the cardiac chambers and valves; its endothelium is continuous with that of vessels entering and leaving the heart.
explanation.whyCorrect: The endocardium is the innermost layer lining the cardiac chambers and valves; its endothelium is continuous with that of vessels entering and leaving the heart.

questions.stem: In this diagram of the heart wall and pericardium, which labeled structure corresponds to the epicardium?

explanation.summary: The epicardium is the visceral layer of the serous pericardium, adherent to the outer surface of the myocardium; the pericardial cavity separates it from the parietal layer.
explanation.whyCorrect: The epicardium is the visceral layer of the serous pericardium, adherent to the outer surface of the myocardium; the pericardial cavity separates it from the parietal layer.

questions.stem: At the inner surface of this heart wall, the subendocardial layer (SEn) beneath the endocardium (En) contains clusters of large, pale-staining cells (P) with abundant clear cytoplasm sitting above the myocardium (M). What are these pale cells?

explanation.summary: Large, pale cells rich in glycogen within the subendocardial layer are Purkinje fibers, specialized conducting cardiomyocytes that rapidly distribute the electrical impulse to the ventricular myocardium.
explanation.whyCorrect: Large, pale cells rich in glycogen within the subendocardial layer are Purkinje fibers, specialized conducting cardiomyocytes that rapidly distribute the electrical impulse to the ventricular myocardium.
